html: † [מְנַעֲנֵעַ] n.[m.] appar. a kind of rattle, only וּבִמְנַֽעַנְעִים 2 S 6:5, in list of musical instruments; 𝔊 κύμβαλα, but this usually (12 times) = מְצִלְתַּיִם; 𝔙 sistra; the sistrum (Gr. σεῖστρον, from σείω) was much used in Egypt; it was a small metal frame with loose metal bars carrying loose rings, borne and swung or shaken in the hand, v. WilkinsonAnc. Egyptians (1878), i. 497 ff. NowArch. 1, 273 BenzArch. 278 We ψψ Eng. Trans. p. 233.
